s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological findings of dense diffuse infiltrate with lymphocytes, histiocytes, and fungal forms
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient has well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years
No systemic complaints
No history of high-risk behavior for HIV
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Histopathological examination showed dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and other cells
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo were found in histiocytes and giant cells
Special stains highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo found in histiocytes, consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Oral histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Nonhealing ulcer on the tongue with histopathological findings of intracellular yeasts, consistent with oral histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of intracellular yeasts and granulomatous inflammation, which can be seen in cryptococcosis

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of epithelioid cells, which can be seen in tuberculosis

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of giant cells, which can be seen in sarcoidosis

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo in histiocytes and giant cells, along with the patient's geographical location in eastern India, supports the diagnosis of oral histoplasmosis.

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: While histoplasmosis is a possible diagnosis, the specific presentation of a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue with intracellular yeasts suggests a more specific diagnosis of oral histoplasmosis.

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: The lack of evidence of cryptococcal forms in the histopathological examination and the negative fungal culture make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Tuberculosis
rejected.why: The absence of underlying induration, friability, or bleeding on manipulation, and the presence of intracellular yeasts, do not support a diagnosis of tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The presence of intracellular yeasts and the specific geographical location of the patient do not support a diagnosis of sarcoidosis, which is characterized by non-caseating granulomas without fungal elements.
